A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLDS research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, experiments, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic parameter-recovery experiments, analyses of mouse and macaque recordings, and model comparisons in Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and adds a neural-circuit simulation, noise and dimensionality studies, and gpSLDS comparison results.

M1.justification: The proposed CLDS retains condition-dependent affine dynamics and emissions, finite-basis GP priors, Kalman smoothing, and MAP estimation through EM. The new neural-circuit model generates evaluation data; it is not a new CLDS component.

E1.justification: v2 adds a nonlinear, 32-unit neural-circuit ring-attractor simulation generated outside the CLDS family (Sections 3.3 and B.3). This extends head-direction coverage to a model-mismatch scenario while retaining the original synthetic task and both biological datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 4e adds gpSLDS to the macaque comparison, retaining LDS and LFADS. gpSLDS was discussed but not evaluated in v1. Although its feature map accommodates rSLDS-like partitions, rSLDS is not reported as a separate comparator.

E3.justification: Added protocols sweep four observation-noise levels and latent dimensions D = 3, 5, 10, 15; the noise study measures eigenvalue-recovery error over 50 angular conditions. The new gpSLDS comparator uses D = 2 because of memory limits. Existing trial splits, primary co-smoothing metric, and LFADS training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained tuning-width recovery and kernel search, v2 adds substantive tests of observation-noise sensitivity (Table 1), latent-dimensionality sensitivity (Table 2), and recovery under a non-CLDS data-generating process (Figure 7). These substantially expand the questions tested about robustness and model adequacy.

E5.justification: The new dimensionality study reports averaging over two random seeds (Table 2). Figure 4 retains five initialization seeds and standard-deviation error bars. This adds run-count information without establishing increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 4e revises the plotted CLDS, LDS, and LFADS scores and adds gpSLDS, while retaining CLDS's lead there. New Table 1 reports co-smoothing R2 declining from 0.99 to 0.21 across increasing noise. Table 2 reports CLDS/LDS scores of 0.232/0.193 at D = 5 and 0.168/0.170 at D = 15. Figure 7 adds recovered circuit dynamics.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 adds an elementwise derivation of the basis-space/Kronecker representation. v2 also removes an extra -W_b term from the intermediate EM likelihood derivative (v1 Equation 19; v2 Equation 15). The final joint update, approximation-error bounds, and SLDS moment-matching derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central claims about interpretability, tractable inference, expressivity, and data efficiency. The conclusion retains the GP-prior and closed-form-inference contribution; the added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the circuit experiment as evidence of recovery under model mismatch and explains why sufficiently large basis counts mainly increase computation rather than statistical complexity. The conclusion also foregrounds Gaussian-only experiments and incomplete parameter-posterior inference as limitations.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with gpSLDS code and configuration, circuit-simulation discretization, mouse-data access instructions, and hardware, memory, and runtime disclosures. It newly specifies four-bin smoothing for mouse recordings; this is additional documentation, not an established preprocessing change. The CLDS repository link is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to dLDS and Input Switched Affine Networks, plus citations on ring-attractor circuits, Markovian GPs, and Fourier approximations. The existing positioning around Wishart processes, GPFA, switching systems, and observed covariates remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative structure is retained, with local rewrites and clarifications in methods, related work, and limitations. A circuit-experiment subsection and additional appendix subsections are inserted. Conference and correspondence text change, and v1's Impact Statement is omitted.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from two columns to a single-column NeurIPS layout. Figure 1 adds condition-to-emission arrows and affine labels; Figure 4 rearranges panels and expands its comparison legend. Figure 7 and Tables 1–2 are new, while other retained figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The non-CLDS circuit example and noise/dimensionality studies provide useful validation missing from v1, and expanded data-access and computing details improve reproducibility. These are targeted gains within the existing applications. The added gpSLDS comparison is informative but limited by its two-dimensional latent space versus five dimensions for the main CLDS reaching model.
